request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

A glass tube of uniform internal radius (r) has a valve separating the two identical ends. Initially, the valve is in a tightly closed position. End 1 has a hemispherial soap bubble of radius r . End 2 has sub-hemispherical soap bubble as shown in figure.
Just after opening the valve.
(A) air from end 1 flows towards end 2 . No change in the volume of the soap bubbles
(B) air from end 1 flows towards end 2. Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 decreases
(C) no change occurs
(D) air from end 2 flows towards end 1 . Volume of the soap bubble at end 1 increases

result.value: Air flows from end 1 to end 2, and the volume of bubble 1 decreases.
result.working: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is ΔP = 4T/R, where R is the radius of curvature of the film. Bubble 1 is a hemisphere on the tube mouth, so its radius equals r, the smallest radius possible there. Bubble 2 is sub-hemispherical, so its radius of curvature is R > r. Therefore P1 = P0 + 4T/r is greater than P2 = P0 + 4T/R. When the valve opens, air flows from end 1 to end 2. Bubble 1 loses air, so its volume decreases.
result.note: The figure is not provided. I assumed the standard setup: bubble 2 is a sub-hemispherical cap on the same tube mouth, so its radius of curvature is larger than r.
